problem: Centralized LLM routing systems lack flexibility and fail to adapt when new models are added or when models have variable performance across different domains.
approach: DiSRouter shifts routing from a centralized external router to distributed agents; each LLM independently judges whether it can answer a query or should route to peers based on its own self-awareness of competence.
contribution: DiSRouter outperforms existing routing methods in utility across scenarios, effectively distinguishes easy from hard queries, and generalizes to out-of-domain tasks.

problem: Graph Neural Networks for multi-agent pathfinding rely on pairwise message passing, which fails to capture group coordination and causes attention dilution in dense environments.
approach: HMAGAT uses hypergraph neural networks with attention mechanisms over directed hypergraphs to explicitly model group dynamics and higher-order agent interactions beyond pairwise relationships.
contribution: HMAGAT achieves state-of-the-art results with only 1M parameters trained on 100x less data than competing methods, while empirically demonstrating that hypergraph representations mitigate attention dilution.

problem: Existing LLM safety benchmarks focus on single-turn dialogues or single jailbreak methods and don't assess models' ability to identify and handle unsafe information in multi-turn contexts.
approach: SafeDialBench provides a two-tier hierarchical safety taxonomy with 6 dimensions, generates 4000+ multi-turn dialogues in Chinese and English under 22 scenarios, and applies 7 jailbreak strategies.
contribution: Evaluations across 19 LLMs reveal that Yi-34B-Chat and GLM4-9B-Chat demonstrate superior safety performance, while Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and o3-mini exhibit vulnerabilities.

problem: Existing diffusion and autoregressive policies suffer from slow inference and struggle with non-Markovian robotic manipulation tasks that require coherent action prediction.
approach: Masked Generative Policy represents actions as discrete tokens and trains a conditional masked transformer for parallel token generation with rapid refinement of low-confidence tokens; MGP-Long predicts full trajectories and refines them dynamically.
contribution: MGP increases average success rate by 9% across 150 Meta-World and LIBERO tasks while reducing inference time by up to 35x, and improves dynamic environment success by 60% where prior methods fail.

problem: Bayesian deep learning lacks a principled way to initialize prior beliefs over model parameters when no natural prior exists.
approach: The model learns weights priors from a collection of datasets via per-dataset amortized variational inference, treating it as a neural process where the latent variable is the BNN weights and the decoder is the network itself.
contribution: The approach enables Bayesian neural networks with well-specified priors, their use as flexible generative models, and enables meta-learning under extreme data starvation.

problem: RLVR approaches struggle to improve reasoning on inherently difficult tasks due to sparse rewards and inefficient learning from both easy and hard tasks simultaneously.
approach: E2H Reasoner schedules tasks from easy to hard, allowing LLMs to build reasoning skills gradually, with theoretical convergence guarantees within an approximate policy iteration framework.
contribution: E2H Reasoner substantially enhances LLM reasoning by deriving convergence bounds showing curriculum-based learning requires fewer total samples than direct learning across diverse datasets and models.

problem: Vision-language models achieve high classification accuracy on standard medical benchmarks but fail at high-stakes clinical reasoning with multimodal data.
approach: Neural-MedBench integrates multi-sequence MRI, structured electronic health records, and clinical notes across three task families (differential diagnosis, lesion recognition, rationale generation) with hybrid scoring combining LLM-based graders and clinician validation.
contribution: Systematic evaluation reveals reasoning failures dominate model shortcomings compared to conventional datasets, establishing the necessity of depth-oriented compact benchmarks for reliable clinical reasoning assessment.

problem: Low-rank compression methods compress each layer independently, causing reconstruction errors to propagate and accumulate through the network, amplifying global deviations.
approach: SAES-SVD jointly optimizes intra-layer reconstruction and inter-layer error compensation via Cumulative Error-Aware Layer Compression (CEALC) and Adaptive Collaborative Error Suppression (ACES), deriving closed-form solutions based on activation statistics.
contribution: SAES-SVD explicitly aligns each compressed layer's output with full-precision counterparts, compensating for accumulated errors across the network.

problem: Diffusion language model post-training methods remain largely unexplored, and their preference-inference trajectories are not aligned with post-training objectives.
approach: TraceRL incorporates inference trajectory information into reinforcement learning for both full-attention and block-attention diffusion models, with a diffusion-based value model that accommodates process rewards.
contribution: TraceRL-derived TraDo models outperform autoregressive baselines: TraDo-4B outperforms Qwen2.5-7B on complex math (4.5% MATH500 gain), and TraDo-8B achieves 6.6% higher accuracy than Llama3.1-8B on coding tasks.

problem: 3D human motion generation models lack generalization capability despite video generation achieving strong transfer learning across domains.
approach: ViMoGen systematically transfers knowledge from video generation to motion generation via: ViMoGen-228k dataset with 228,000 samples combining MoCap, web videos, and synthetic ViGen outputs; a flow-matching diffusion transformer with gated multimodal conditioning; and a hierarchical MBench for evaluation.
contribution: ViMoGen significantly outperforms existing motion generation approaches in both automatic and human evaluations across quality, prompt fidelity, and generalization.

problem: Task vector merging for balancing accuracy and robustness creates a near-linear trade-off because it equally weights all parameters without identifying coordinates that support both objectives.
approach: A stability-aware merging framework uses prediction stability as a proxy for cross-objective compatibility, building masks that retain jointly stable parameters while suppressing those with high cross-objective impact, refined along adversarial trajectories.
contribution: The framework provably contracts first-order cross-objective interference and bias toward flatter minima, enabling better balance of clean and robust performance without retraining.

problem: Finding dense correspondences across human head images is challenged by pose variations, hair coverage, and the need for high-quality geometric understanding.
approach: DenseMarks trains a Vision Transformer to predict 3D embeddings for each pixel corresponding to locations in a canonical unit cube, using point tracks from talking head videos with contrastive loss, supplemented by face landmarks and segmentation multi-task learning.
contribution: DenseMarks achieves state-of-the-art geometry-aware point matching and monocular head tracking with 3D Morphable Models, robust to pose variations with consistent representations across diverse individuals.

problem: Point cloud representation learning struggles to simultaneously capture intricate local structures and global contextual dependencies.
approach: PointLearner uses point-focused attention simulating foveal vision with competitive normalized attention between local neighbors and downsampled features, combined with a context-scan state space mimicking saccadic eye movements via Hilbert curve guidance.
contribution: PointLearner achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple point cloud tasks with remarkable robustness, demonstrating the effectiveness of biomimetic focus-then-context design.

problem: It is unclear how post-training in language models causes model shifts that affect domain transfer, making it difficult to predict downstream performance before expensive fine-tuning.
approach: SAE-based Transferability Score (STS) uses sparse autoencoders to identify shifted dimensions in SAE representations and calculate their correlations with downstream domains, enabling transferability prediction before fine-tuning.
contribution: STS accurately predicts supervised fine-tuning transferability with Pearson correlation above 0.75 with actual performance changes, serving as an interpretable tool for guiding post-training strategies.

problem: Human-in-the-loop AI designs vary in structure and safety implications, yet lack formal characterization or clear legal accountability frameworks.
approach: Uses computability theory and oracle machines to formalize HITL setups (trivial monitoring, single-endpoint actions, Turing reductions), identifies failure modes, and analyzes legal/ethical responsibility gaps in UK/EU frameworks.
contribution: Reveals an unavoidable trade-off between legal responsibility attribution and technical explainability, showing HITL involves design decisions prone to failures beyond human control.

problem: Vector quantization's hard assignments block gradients and prevent end-to-end training, requiring auxiliary losses or temperature schedules.
approach: DiVeQ treats quantization as adding an error vector mimicking quantization distortion while keeping the forward pass hard, enabling gradient flow without auxiliary losses; SF-DiVeQ uses space-filling curves connecting codewords for better coverage.
contribution: DiVeQ improves reconstruction and sample quality over alternative quantization approaches on VQ-VAE and VQGAN across datasets without requiring auxiliary losses or temperature schedules.

problem: Existing LLM workflow benchmarks don't systematically evaluate performance under realistic tool failure patterns and variable instruction quality.
approach: PILOT-Bench incorporates parameterized error models simulating real API failures, provides MDP-derived workflows, and systematically evaluates robustness through controlled instruction quality perturbations, generating 5,040 tasks from 30 APIs.
contribution: Evaluations reveal MDP-optimal prompts achieve 62.1% success rate, Chain-of-Thought yields 50.8%, and flawed prompts achieve 54.3%, showing significant performance differences under uncertainty.

problem: Automatic tool generation agents fail to adapt effectively to long-horizon, stateful office tasks requiring coherent world modeling and persistent state tracking.
approach: ROGA introduces Active World Modeling to probe environments and construct internal models, Persistent Symbolic Memory tracking state evolution, and Dynamic Capability Evolution for meta-learning; applied to office ecosystem tasks.
contribution: ROGA addresses fundamental paradigm limitations, showing current ATG agents underperform by up to 27.43%, and demonstrates ROGA's effectiveness on long-horizon office productivity benchmarks.

problem: Designing memory-efficient optimizers for LLMs that maintain fast convergence is challenging, and efficient optimizer design lacks systematic guidance.
approach: Proposes structured Fisher information matrix approximation as a lens for optimizer design, derives design recommendations through careful structural assumptions, and introduces low-rank extension framework for efficiency.
contribution: New optimizers RACS and Alice achieve 2x faster convergence than Adam on 1B LLaMA with comparable or better memory efficiency, validating systematic Fisher-based design approach.

problem: Neural scaling laws focus on generalization but do not explain how inference scaling (pass@k) depends on training, especially under instance heterogeneous difficulty.
approach: The Latent Instance Difficulty model captures heavy-tailed target variance distributions, showing pass@k failure rate exhibits power-law decay k^(-β_eff) where β_eff grows with training before saturating.
contribution: Learning shrinks the hard tail of error distributions; provides closed-form predictions for scaling behavior and compute-allocation rules favoring training before saturation, validated on CIFAR-10H and distillation tasks.

problem: Existing membership inference attacks on diffusion models assume access to ground-truth captions, which fails when only images are available and annotations are unknown.
approach: MoFit constructs synthetic conditioning inputs explicitly overfitted to the model's generative manifold through model-fitted surrogate optimization, then extracts embeddings for membership classification without ground-truth captions.
contribution: MoFit consistently outperforms VLM-conditioned baselines across datasets and diffusion models, enabling caption-free privacy auditing when annotations are unavailable.

problem: Diffusion language models suffer from slow inference due to multiple full-sequence forward passes in denoising, and parallel token generation causes token incoherence.
approach: FreeCache reuses stable key-value projections across denoising steps; Guided Diffusion uses a lightweight pretrained autoregressive model to supervise token unmasking, reducing denoising iterations without quality loss.
contribution: Combined techniques deliver 12.14x end-to-end speedup with negligible accuracy degradation, achieving comparable latency to autoregressive models for the first time.

problem: Convergence analysis of actor-critic methods for entropy-regularized MDPs in continuous spaces with unbounded regularizers lacks stability guarantees.
approach: Proves stability and convergence of coupled actor-critic gradient flow with separate timescales: critic uses temporal difference learning, policy uses policy mirror descent on unbounded relative entropy.
contribution: Establishes stability preventing finite-time blow-up and derives convergence rate to optimal regularized value function, showing timescale separation is crucial for stability.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models for autonomous driving lack interpretability and coherence in their decision-making and may produce implausible action sequences.
approach: AutoDrive-R² enhances reasoning via chain-of-thought processing with self-reflection, and uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with physics-grounded rewards capturing spatial alignment, vehicle dynamics, and temporal smoothness.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes and Waymo datasets with robust generalization and improved interpretability through reasoning and self-reflection.

problem: The complexity landscape and algorithmic tractability of non-clashing teaching for closed neighborhoods in graphs remains unexplored.
approach: Studies positive non-clashing teaching for closed neighborhoods in graphs, providing FPT algorithms for restricted parameters and deriving combinatorial bounds for wider graph classes.
contribution: Yields improved algorithmic results with FPT algorithms for more general parameter classes and stronger lower bounds compared to prior work on balls in graphs.

problem: Existing vision-language models lack the ability to iteratively refine understanding across multiple visual regions through multi-round reasoning.
approach: RegionReasoner enforces grounded reasoning via reinforcement learning where each trace cites reference bounding boxes, maintaining semantic coherence through global-local consistency rewards.
contribution: Considerably improves multi-round reasoning accuracy, spatial grounding precision, and global-local consistency on detection and segmentation tasks with RegionDial-Bench benchmark.

problem: Gradient descent for training PINNs suffers from poor convergence dependence on sample size and Gram matrix eigenvalues, leading to slow training.
approach: Shows NGD enables maximal learning rates of O(1) independent of Gram matrix properties; demonstrates quadratic convergence for smooth activation functions via positive definiteness of general Gram matrices.
contribution: Provides convergence analysis of natural gradient descent for two-layer PINNs, showing independence from Gram matrix conditioning and achieving improved convergence rates.

problem: Existing driving-scene generation methods struggle to support high-quality novel-view synthesis due to limited 3D consistency and sparse viewpoint coverage.
approach: WorldSplat introduces a feed-forward framework combining a 4D-aware latent diffusion model that generates pixel-aligned 4D Gaussians with enhanced video diffusion for refinement.
contribution: Generates high-fidelity, temporally and spatially consistent multi-track novel view driving videos supporting convenient scene generation and reconstruction.

problem: Joint model compression combining multiple methods lacks understanding of compression order effects, and prior work assumes orthogonality between techniques.
approach: Formulates compression order optimization problem, introduces Progressive Intensity Hypothesis stating weaker perturbations should precede stronger ones, provides theoretical guarantees and empirical validation.
contribution: Shows relative benefit of compression order increases with underlying performance gap; validates hypothesis across language and vision models and multi-stage compression scenarios.

problem: Flow matching density estimators often fail to explicitly capture rich latent structure in complex data.
approach: Structured Flow Autoencoders augments Continuous Normalizing Flows with graphical models, using a novel flow matching objective that explicitly accounts for latent variables enabling simultaneous likelihood and posterior learning.
contribution: SFA outperforms VAEs and graphical model extensions, achieving better data fit while retaining meaningful latent variables as structured representations.

problem: The structures in data enabling in-context learning emergence and governing its robustness remain poorly understood, particularly under train-test task mismatch.
approach: Studies pretraining-testing task alignment in ICL using a solvable model of linear regression by linear attention, deriving exact generalization error expressions under arbitrary task covariance mismatch.
contribution: Identifies train-test task alignment as key ICL generalization determinant, revealing trade-off between specialization and generalization depending on task distribution alignment.

problem: Existing LLM fingerprinting methods extract signatures only after training begins, making them unreliable early in training and vulnerable to distribution shifts.
approach: SeedPrints leverages random initialization biases as seed-dependent fingerprints present before training, using time-contrastive learning to enhance temporal distinctiveness of moment tokens.
contribution: Achieves seed-level distinguishability with effectiveness across all training stages and robustness under domain shifts, providing birth-to-lifecycle identity verification.

problem: Current AI systems struggle with precise molecular recognition, editing, and generation even for intuitively simple chemistry tasks.
approach: MolLangBench evaluates fundamental molecule-language interface tasks using automated cheminformatics for recognition, expert annotation for editing/generation, supporting linear strings, molecular images, and graphs.
contribution: Shows strongest model (GPT-5) achieves only 86.2% and 85.5% on recognition and editing, and 43.0% on generation, revealing significant limitations in molecular manipulation.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, and existing attacks require full model gradients or elaborate transfer strategies with large perturbations.
approach: VEAttack targets only the vision encoder (gray-box) by perturbing patch tokens rather than class tokens, minimizing cosine similarity between clean and perturbed visual features without downstream model access.
contribution: Achieves 94.5% performance degradation on image captioning and 75.7% on VQA with reduced computational overhead and no task/label dependence, revealing attention differential and Möbius band in transfer attacks.

problem: Simultaneous Navigation and Mapping typically requires global map construction, which is computationally expensive and not biologically plausible.
approach: GRL-SNAM formulates navigation and mapping as coupled dynamics on generalized Hamiltonian manifolds, using local energy landscapes encoding reachability and obstacles, with policies evolving through Differential Policy Optimization.
contribution: Superior path quality with minimal map coverage on 2D deformable navigation, preserves clearance, generalizes to unseen environments, demonstrating efficient local exploration via Hamiltonian-structured RL.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action models ignore historical context and are designed for single-observation action prediction, limiting performance on history-dependent manipulation tasks.
approach: HAMLET adds moment tokens encoding temporal information initialized via time-contrastive learning, integrated across past timesteps by a lightweight memory module for history-aware action prediction.
contribution: On GR00T N1.5 baseline, achieves 76.4% success on history-dependent tasks (47.2% improvement), pushes RoboCasa from 64.1% to 66.4%, and LIBERO from 95.6% to 97.7%.

problem: Deterministic concept bottleneck mappings in generative models are susceptible to concept leakage, limiting steerability and direct generation from specified concepts.
approach: Variational Hard Concept Bottleneck (VHCB) layer maps probabilistic binary latent variables to hard concepts, enabling direct generation from specified concepts and mitigating leakage.
contribution: VHCB consistently improves steerability across various tasks like concept activation/deactivation with systematic evaluation framework for CBGM steerability assessment.

problem: Existing skill learning for LLM agents creates over-specialized skills bound to single websites and fail to generalize across environments.
approach: PolySkill decouples skill's abstract goal from concrete implementation inspired by software polymorphism, enabling agents to learn generalizable and compositional skills.
contribution: Improves skill reuse by 1.7x on seen websites, boosts success rates by up to 9.4% on Mind2Web and 13.9% on unseen websites while reducing steps by 20%.

problem: Existing LLM-based traffic signal control treats intersections independently without inter-intersection cooperation, limiting network-wide optimization.
approach: CoLLMLight enables agents to perform in-depth spatiotemporal reasoning through asynchronous cooperative decision architecture, with cost-aware cooperation optimization and adaptive reasoning chain depth.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods on four real-world traffic networks, achieving more effective and generalizable cooperation while maintaining real-time responsiveness.

problem: Deep neural networks exhibit substantial class-wise accuracy disparities even on class-balanced data, hindering reliable deployment.
approach: MR² applies dynamically adjusted margins in logit and representation spaces based on per-class feature variability, with novel margin-based class-sensitive generalization bounds.
contribution: Improves overall accuracy and significantly boosts hard class performance without trading off easy classes across seven datasets including ImageNet with diverse pre-trained backbones.
